title:
Your first paycheque.
Your first little choice.
body: Meet Maya. You’re 19, studying, and working part-time. Your first paycheque is in! After the essentials, you have $500 left. What will you do with it?

choices.title: Enjoy a little right now
choices.description: Spend $400 on a weekend with friends.

title:
New semester.
New laptop.
body: Your old laptop has given up, and you need one for class. A reliable replacement costs $800. Your next two monthly surpluses have arrived. How will you pay?

title:
An unexpected turn.
A $900 repair.
body: Your car needs a repair to get you to work. This is the kind of surprise an emergency fund is for. How would you like to cover the bill?

choices.title: Let your cushion catch you
choices.description: Use emergency savings first, then cash.

choices.title: A little savings, a little credit
choices.description: Use available emergency savings; borrow the rest.

choices.title: Cover it with your card
choices.description: Add the full $900 to your credit balance.

title:
A little money.
A bigger possibility.
body: You have $900 to put toward your future. Money for a goal this year needs a different home from money you can leave invested for years. Where will yours go?

choices.title: Keep it for a near-term goal
choices.description: Set aside $900 in cash for next year’s tuition.

choices.title: Back one big idea
choices.description: Invest all $900 in the fictional technology sector.

choices.title: Give your money three homes
choices.description: Invest $300 each in technology, energy, and retail.

title:
Markets have seasons.
This one is stormy.
body: A fictional downturn has reached town: technology falls 35%, energy 8%, and retail 12%. Your balances already include these changes. What happens next is a choice, too.

choices.title: Bring your investments home
choices.description: Sell at today’s value and hold the proceeds in cash.

choices.title: Give your plan more time
choices.description: Keep your current allocation through December.
